feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the experience progression is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with the target title. Writing is polished overall, but impact would improve with more outcome-focused metrics, less repetition across skills sections, and a few consistency edits.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, showing increasing leadership, ownership, and strategic scope over time.  
- Strong domain credibility: Drupal, analytics, governance, multimedia, and advocacy/public-sector communications are all well evidenced.  
- Good use of scale indicators (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers), which strengthens seniority and impact.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond scope: include performance gains, engagement improvements, efficiency savings, revenue/support for campaigns, or adoption results. Several bullets describe responsibilities more than achievements.  
- Reduce duplication and tighten structure: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve scannability and save space.  
- Fix style/consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; use serial commas consistently (“workflows and systems” vs. “workflows, systems, and…”); “A2/Learning” is awkward—use “French (A2, currently learning).” No major misspellings or obvious typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It reads clearly, but it’s slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, more standard phrasing.
- Lead with your strongest differentiators: enterprise web modernization, cross-channel strategy, and mission-driven/public-sector communications.
- Add a clearer leadership signal by referencing digital operations, governance, or team/program leadership.
- Tighten wording to reduce abstraction: “building the workflows and systems” → “designing workflows, governance, and systems.”

Possible rewrite:
Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel communications, enterprise web modernization, and digital operations, including the workflows, governance, and systems that support complex teams. Strong background in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and workflow/systems language overlap with Core Competencies; keep the intro higher-level.
- “Advocacy messaging” is reinforced throughout NACo roles, so avoid adding more detail here.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the summary, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. It would be sharper if it emphasized higher-value leadership capabilities and used more parallel, specific phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use consistent noun phrases and tighten wording: “Multi-channel communications,” “Stakeholder coordination,” “Web platform administration.”
- Prioritize strategic, senior-level strengths over generic tasks; consider: Digital strategy & platform modernization • Editorial systems & governance • Multi-channel communications leadership • Web platform & CMS administration • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Cross-functional stakeholder coordination • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia & live event production
- Replace “Workflow & systems architecture” with “Editorial systems & workflow design” if you want clearer alignment to your experience.
- Consider dropping one lower-priority item to keep the list more focused and scannable.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills and the summary.
- “Digital strategy,” “analytics,” “multimedia,” and “policy/advocacy communication” are already covered in Topline Skills and the header.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list. Tighten the opening, foreground the highest-impact work, and add outcomes or scale to distinguish it from your NACo entries.

Suggested edit
- Replace the opening with a sharper summary: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital strategy, Drupal-based campaign delivery, and enterprise web improvement.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one impact-oriented bullet; e.g., “Built cross-functional content operations, analytics, and governance workflows to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make the Drupal/CMS bullet more outcome-driven: mention number of sites, users, launches, turnaround time, or publishing efficiency if available.
- Recast the AI search bullet as a flagship achievement: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval strategy, structured content requirements, and discovery UX to improve findability.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, and digital operations” overlaps with NACo; keep this entry focused on consulting scope, Drupal delivery, and AI search.
- “CMS development/front-end implementation” may duplicate skills sections; emphasize business impact, not just tools.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It would be even stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation wins, and add clearer outcome language beyond platform size.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad first sentence with a sharper scope statement: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Reorder bullets to emphasize biggest wins first: website migration, analytics modernization, video studio build, then channel leadership/governance.
- Strengthen outcomes where possible: add % improvements, cost savings, production volume, engagement growth, reporting speed, or reduced reliance on vendors/freelancers.
- Tighten channel bullet: “Oversaw email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social channels engaging thousands of followers” rather than listing “core digital communications channels.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led digital communications across web, email, social media and video” overlaps with the prior NACo role; keep this entry focused on director-level transformation, infrastructure, and team leadership.
- “Governance/publishing standards/workflows” also appears elsewhere; use only if you can show a distinct enterprise-level impact.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story within NACo, but this entry overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing executional leadership, editorial operations, and channel growth before the broader strategic ownership in the next role.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to focus on scope and function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media, and video, strengthening editorial coordination and advocacy messaging.”
- Tighten bullets and use stronger verbs: “Oversaw four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Clarify impact where possible: add open rates, subscriber growth, video views, production volume, or workflow improvements if available.
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper outcome-oriented line: “Built cross-team editorial planning and standardized publishing workflows across communications, advocacy, and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role’s “weekly video updates.”
- “Improved digital publishing workflows” is very close to the 2022–2024 role’s governance/publishing standards language.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning

Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and avoid generic phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad labels with sharper, leadership-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation
- Editorial governance, workflow design & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, policy & advocacy communications
- Audience strategy, content planning & message architecture
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel communications leadership” for “Cross-channel communications leadership” to align with the header while sounding more current.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is weak/generic; strengthen to “Audience strategy, content planning & message architecture.”
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this category to scale/results from recent roles rather than listing only concepts.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats “digital strategy,” “editorial workflow,” “multi-channel communication,” and “advocacy communication” already stated in the header and Core Competencies.
- “Editorial systems and governance” also overlaps with NACo bullets on governance, publishing standards, and planning systems.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant mix of platforms and execution skills, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize current, high-value capabilities and group them more strategically.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a software list to a capability-led line, e.g.: “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint & Power Pages • CMS modernization & migration • Front-end web implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations & workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery”
- Put Drupal first and keep AI-enabled search near the end to reflect recent, differentiated work.
- Replace “Airtable systems” with “Airtable-based systems” or “Airtable workflow systems” for clearer value.
- If space allows, swap “technical execution” language toward outcomes: “CMS modernization & migration” and “content discovery” are stronger than generic platform names.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This heavily duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and let the later section carry the full tool inventory.
- “Workflow automation” also overlaps with Core Competencies and Technical + IT.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack for recent leadership roles, but this item reads as a generic list. It would be stronger if it emphasized decision-making, measurement, and optimization outcomes rather than just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Digital analytics, reporting & optimization” or “Analytics strategy, dashboards & performance insights.”
- Group tools with outcomes: “GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, and BigQuery for KPI design, executive reporting, and performance analysis.”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with a sharper phrase like “executive dashboards” or “decision-ready reporting.”
- Consider adding one higher-value capability such as “measurement framework development” or “conversion/performance optimization” if accurate.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with “Data analytics & reporting” in Core Competencies and the NACo bullet on expanding analytics infrastructure; keep this section concise and tool/capability-focused rather than repeating impact claims.
- “SEO and performance analysis” may feel slightly tacked on unless SEO appears elsewhere in experience.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

Quick assessment: Strong supporting skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia & live event production” in Core Competencies plus multiple NACo experience bullets. Make it more specific, senior, and operations-focused.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from task list to capability cluster: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio system operation • Virtual event production workflows”

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and doesn’t show depth or recency. This section should either be tighter or add light qualification to emphasize strongest/current platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize current/relevant tools first: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider signaling strength: “Drupal (enterprise) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- If space allows, group by level of use: “Drupal (primary) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; use “CMS & Web Platforms” if you want slightly clearer labeling.
- Only include GitHub Pages if you’ve used it meaningfully in recent work; otherwise replace with a more relevant platform or drop it.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section almost exactly.
- “Web & CMS administration” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating the same list elsewhere unless differentiated by proficiency.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool list, but it reads as a generic keyword dump and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should feel more implementation-focused and current, not repeat broader skills already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit
- Rename to emphasize applied capability: “Front-End & Technical Implementation” or “Web Development & Automation.”
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: “HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions.”
- If accurate, add scope or outcomes instead of only tools, e.g. “Built front-end components, implemented API-based integrations, deployed edge scripts via Cloudflare Workers, and automated workflows with GitHub Actions.”
- Consider dropping versioned labels (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless needed; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Strong overlap with Topline Skills: “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery,” “API integrations,” and “Workflow automation.”
- “GitHub Actions” may fit better under “Automation & Workflow Systems” unless you specifically used it for deployment/dev workflows.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is too tool-list heavy and overlaps with stronger positioning already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. It should emphasize automation/system-building tools and de-emphasize generic collaboration apps.

Suggested edit:
- Narrow to tools that support your recent workflow/automation work: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana”
- Move Slack, Teams, and Basecamp/Trello out unless they are required by the target role; they read as everyday collaboration tools, not differentiating technical systems skills.
- Consider retitling to sharpen relevance: “Workflow Automation & Project Systems” or “Automation, Workflow & PM Systems”
- If space allows, add light qualifiers instead of a pure list, e.g. “Airtable (workflow databases), Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same language verbatim.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp are partially redundant with your demonstrated leadership in editorial planning and cross-team coordination in recent roles.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as generic software inventory rather than evidence of email/engagement capability. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and tool-focused.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten the line to: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add one higher-value qualifier instead of more tools, e.g. **campaign automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation**
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV: use either **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys** or the exact product branding you used professionally, not a slash-heavy variant unless required

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding outcomes like newsletter reach or campaign leadership here; those are already covered in recent NACo experience
- Don’t repeat “email newsletters” language from Work Experience; this section should remain platform/stack-oriented

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but the item is too general and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize “firsts,” production scope, and team-building support.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground concrete contributions: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and support daily execution across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add clearer outcomes if available: website refresh scope, livestream/event volume, cadence/audience for weekly video updates, or workflow improvements (faster publishing, better coordination, expanded output).
- Tighten phrasing and reduce stacked verbs: replace “supporting the creation… and strengthening workflows” with one direct accomplishment plus one operational result.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team, support a major website refresh, and produce recurring multimedia content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while helping coordinate day-to-day publishing workflows and mentoring a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; differentiate this entry by emphasizing launch/early buildout.
- “Strengthening workflows” repeats language used elsewhere; specify what changed or omit.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed as a foundation for later digital/media leadership, with less generic “coordinated/contributed” language.

Suggested edit
- Replace broad phrasing with clearer ownership: “Managed innovation and research projects supporting NACo program and policy initiatives.”
- Elevate the standout achievement: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- Combine digital/media work into one concise impact line: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support member communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add scope or output metrics: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid overemphasizing multimedia production here; later NACo roles already cover video, livestreams, and digital team growth more strongly.
- “Supporting organizational programs and policy work” is vague and may overlap with later advocacy communications unless made more specific.
